deferred_source_units.source_text: When a person finishes, then he begins; when he stops, then he will be at a loss.
deferred_source_units.reason: The paradox says finishing is beginning and stopping leaves one at a loss. General statements about unsearchable divine works do not independently establish this precise sequence, so the source is deferred without adding an explanatory subject to its wording.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Every understanding person has known wisdom and will give acknowledgment to the one who finds her.
deferred_source_units.reason: The unit specifically joins knowing wisdom with acknowledgment of the person who finds her. The read texts about acquiring wisdom do not establish this particular acknowledgment relationship.

deferred_source_units.source_text: The one who rejoices in heart will be condemned,
deferred_source_units.reason: The native text says the one rejoicing in heart will be condemned. It does not explicitly say rejoicing in sin; a link based on that added qualifier would silently alter the source.

deferred_source_units.source_text: A eunuch’s desire to take a young woman’s virginity—so is the one who carries out judgments by force.
deferred_source_units.reason: The eunuch and virginity comparison is specifically applied to carrying out judgments by force. No read target adequately explains that precise analogy without importing an interpretation of the eunuch or of coercive judgment.

deferred_source_units.source_text: There is a gift that will not benefit you, and a gift whose repayment is double.
deferred_source_units.reason: The contrast includes both a gift without benefit and a gift repaid double. The read warnings about grudging gifts do not substantiate the distinctive double-repayment clause or settle its direction.

deferred_source_units.source_text: There is someone who buys much for little and pays for it sevenfold.
deferred_source_units.reason: Buying much for little and paying sevenfold is a particular reversal in exchange. Neither ordinary debt warnings nor the read theft-restitution text establishes that this purchase is theft or an equivalent transaction.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Those who eat his bread are base in speech. How often, and how many, will laugh at him?
deferred_source_units.reason: The unit describes the fool's bread-eaters as base in speech and asks how many laugh at him. General warnings about foolish speech do not establish this particular relationship between the host, guests, and mockery.

deferred_source_units.source_text: There is someone who makes a promise to a friend because of shame, and has acquired him as an enemy for nothing.
deferred_source_units.reason: The source links shame-induced promising with acquiring a friend as an enemy. It does not specify a financial guarantee; the read warnings about pledges cannot safely be substituted for its unspecified promise.

deferred_source_units.source_text: One who is powerful with the tongue is known from far away, but an understanding person knows when he slips.
deferred_source_units.reason: The contrast pairs far-reaching fame for powerful speech with the understanding person's recognition of his own slip. A general tongue warning does not independently support that particular fame-and-self-recognition contrast.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Wisdom is like a ruined house to a fool, and an uncomprehending person’s knowledge is unexamined words.
deferred_source_units.reason: Wisdom as a ruined house to the fool and knowledge as unexamined words form a distinctive comparison. The read house-building images concern stability or destruction, not this exact description of how the fool regards wisdom.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Fools have their heart in their mouth, but the heart of the wise is their mouth.
deferred_source_units.reason: The native second clause says the heart of the wise is their mouth. The familiar reversed wording about a wise mouth being in the heart was not substituted, and no link requiring that reversal is retained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: When an ungodly person curses Satan, he curses his own soul.
deferred_source_units.reason: The explicit claim that the ungodly person cursing Satan curses his own soul requires an explanatory relationship not stated here. General warnings about cursing do not establish that self-directed consequence.

deferred_source_units.source_text: The one who pricks an eye will bring down tears; the one who pricks a heart reveals feeling.
deferred_source_units.reason: Pricking an eye to produce tears is compared with pricking a heart to reveal feeling. No read target sustains this precise analogy without replacing it with a generic statement about sorrow.

deferred_source_units.source_text: If evil things happen to me because of him, everyone who hears will guard against him.
deferred_source_units.reason: The source specifically predicts public caution about a friend after others hear of harm suffered because of him. The read loyalty and betrayal texts do not establish that particular report-and-warning sequence.

deferred_source_units.source_text: There is an expression comparable to death; let it not be found in Jacob’s inheritance. For all these things will depart from the godly, and they will not wallow in sins.
deferred_source_units.reason: The expression comparable to death is not named in this unit. It was not identified as a particular oath or blasphemy without textual support, and generic condemnation of bad speech is insufficient.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Two kinds multiply sins, and the third will bring wrath:
deferred_source_units.reason: This native unit is the numerical introduction to the examples that follow. It names no particular sinful conduct by itself; an unrelated three-part list would provide only a formal resemblance.

deferred_source_units.source_text: But my soul hated three kinds, and I was greatly offended at their life: a proud poor person, a rich liar, and an old adulterer deficient in understanding.
deferred_source_units.reason: The three disliked types specifically combine poverty with pride, wealth with lying, and old age with adultery. Generic rebukes of those vices do not substantiate this particular threefold combination.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Any wound, but not a wound of the heart; any evil, but not a woman’s evil;
deferred_source_units.reason: The hyperbolic preferences single out a heart wound and a woman's evil. Neither the read passages about marital damage nor faintheartedness matches the stated comparison closely enough to retain a distinct pair.

deferred_source_units.source_text: any calamity, but not a calamity from those who hate; any retribution, but not the retribution of enemies.
deferred_source_units.reason: The repeated preferences intensify calamity from haters and retribution from enemies. General enemy passages do not establish these particular comparisons with every other calamity or retribution.

deferred_source_units.source_text: There is no head beyond a snake’s head, and no anger beyond an enemy’s anger.
deferred_source_units.reason: The snake's head and an enemy's anger are set out as unmatched extremes. No read target sufficiently connects those specific comparisons, and the head was not silently changed to venom.

deferred_source_units.source_text: A woman’s evil changes her appearance and darkens her face like a bear.
deferred_source_units.reason: The image specifically makes a woman's evil alter her appearance and darken her face like a bear. General facial-expression or marital-conflict passages do not support the distinctive bear comparison.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Every evil is small beside a woman’s evil; may a sinner’s lot fall upon her.
deferred_source_units.reason: The unit makes an extreme comparison of evils and invokes a sinner's lot upon the woman. A general warning about a harmful wife would not substantiate either the universal comparison or the curse.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Wrath, shamelessness, and great shame result if a wife supplies her husband.
deferred_source_units.reason: The particular claim attaches wrath and shame to a wife supplying her husband. The read passages about harmful marital conduct do not establish this claim about provision itself.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Do not give water an outlet, or an evil wife freedom of speech.
deferred_source_units.reason: The paired prohibitions concern an outlet for water and freedom of speech for an evil wife. The actual Proverbs 17:14 contains no opening-water image, and a broad speech warning would not establish the source's specific comparison.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: Will not dew bring relief from scorching heat? So a word is better than a gift.

target_units.text: The evil person will certainly not heed it, nor say anything timely and good for the community.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The native text concerns an evil person failing to say something timely and good for the community, not the familiar positive saying that a timely word is good. The retained restorative-word image is Proverbs 16:24.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: Rot and worms will inherit him, and a reckless soul will be taken away.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The native unit describes sin remembering a person and his vanishing like mist, not worms feeding on him. Sirach 10:11 provides the retained actual worm-and-inheritance wording.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: A fool will suffer labor pains over a word, like a woman giving birth over her baby.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The actual proverb says the senseless person is led by foolishness; it does not say that he delights in exposing his heart. Sirach's particular bodily-pressure comparison is linked to the following arrow image instead.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: If lack of strength prevents him from sinning, he will do evil when he finds an opportunity.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The native reason for the evildoers' action is that they did not raise their hands to God, not that power was in their hands. Sirach 20:21 supplies an actual comparison involving circumstances preventing sin.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: A graceless person is an untimely tale; it will be continually in the mouth of the uninstructed.

target_units.text: Thorns grow in the hand of the drunkard, but slavery is in the hand of fools.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The native proverb concerns thorns in a drunkard's hand and slavery in fools' hands. It contains no proverb in a fool's mouth; the proposed familiar-wording association is not retained.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: A lazy person has been compared to a lump of dung; everyone who picks it up will shake his hand.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The native subject compared to harmful grapes and smoke is lawlessness, not a lazy messenger. The exact paired lazy-person images in Sirach 22:1-2 are retained instead.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: An untimely discourse is music in mourning, but lashes and discipline are wisdom at every time.

target_units.text: As vinegar is unsuitable for a wound, so a suffering that falls upon the body pains the heart.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The actual proverb compares vinegar on a wound with bodily suffering that pains the heart. It does not mention singing to a heavy heart, so it does not supply the proposed mourning-and-music counterpart.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: Do not multiply words with a fool or go to someone without understanding. unresolved_candidates.source_text: For first she disobeyed the law of the Most High; second she wronged her husband; and third she committed adultery in sexual immorality and presented children from another man.
